topics.topic: Definition and scope of FIFO admission order, including whether multi-lock requests reserve their later session-lock position
questions: Which event establishes a request's admission order: arrival at the listener, entry into `admit_owner_request`, successful session checking, or ticket assignment while holding the session-table lock?

Does the FIFO promise cover every pair of requests that eventually acquire the same session lock, or only requests already queued for the same particular lock; specifically, may a later non-file change overtake an earlier file-touching request before that earlier request joins the session-lock queue?

For the FIFO promise, does “admitted” mean admission of the request as a whole or entry into each particular lock's queue, and does a request waiting for the import lock already reserve its later place on the session lock?

When an earlier uploaded-file request waits first for the import lock and will later wait for the session lock, does it count as sharing that session lock with a later non-file change, or does “the same lock” mean only the first lock on which requests have already drawn tickets?

quotes:
The arrival is fixed in one hold of the session-table lock
(Conventions, "Locks of an owner request"): this operation reads the clock,
looks the session up, checks it, restarts its 30 minutes and, for a request
that passed and needs a lock, draws its turn — a ticket of the import lock
for a request that touches an uploaded file, a place on the session's lock
for any other change, neither waiting — then releases the table lock and
only then waits for that turn (owner, 2026-11-24); nothing else is held for
the request between its headers and that hold.

A change that touches no
uploaded file thus has its place on the session's lock from its admission;
a request that touches one waits for its ticket of the import lock and then
takes its place, so the locks are always taken
import first and no place on a session's lock waits for the import lock (A16
rule 2).

A change that touches an uploaded
file takes its place only after the import lock, so a later change that
touches none may take its place first; the admission order is kept only
where both the import lock and the session's lock order it, as for a
sign-out (`sign_out_owner`).
judgement.why: The texts define admission as the successful session check and turn assignment in the session-table-lock hold, and explicitly say that a file-touching request reserves only its import-lock ticket until that lock is granted, allowing a later non-file change to take the session-lock place first.
options: Order by successful session checking and ticket assignment under the session-table lock.
An earlier uploaded-file request reserves its later session-lock position immediately.
An uploaded-file request takes its session-lock place only after obtaining the import lock, so a later non-file change may overtake it.
consequences: Concurrent requests are ordered by the turns assigned during admission, with FIFO maintained separately by each lock's assigned tickets or places; a file-touching request does not reserve a future session-lock place while waiting for the import lock.

topics.topic: Which locks ordinary and uploaded-file read requests must acquire
questions: Does this mean that a read takes neither the import lock nor a session lock but still takes the session-table lock for session validation and the last-request update, or literally that it takes no owner-session lock at all?

Does this mean only that an ordinary domain read takes no import or session turn, while every read still takes the session-table lock and a read touching an uploaded file also takes the import and session locks, or are uploaded-file reads intended to be lock-free too?

Does “a read takes no lock” mean that a read takes neither the import lock nor a session lock but still takes the session-table lock for its session check and last-request update, or does it literally take no lock?

for a request that touches an uploaded file, a place on the session's lock
for any other change, neither waiting — then releases the table lock and
only then waits for that turn (owner, 2026-11-24); nothing else is held for
the request between its headers and that hold.

`owner_sessions` also keeps one session-table lock, which guards every
session's entry with its signed-out mark and its last-request reading:
each read or write of them is made under it and only there — a sign-in
adds its session, the session check reads the session and restarts its 30
minutes, a sign-out marks and removes it, the pass reads every session's
readings by its one clock reading and removes those past a limit, and
`give_session_csrf` reads one.
judgement.why: The lock-free-read statement excludes an ordinary read from the import and per-session ordering turns, while the session check and last-request update still occur under the session-table lock and any request that reads an uploaded file takes both the import and session locks.
options: An ordinary read takes only the session-table lock for admission and no import or per-session ordering lock.
A read touching an uploaded file takes the session-table lock for admission and then the import and session locks.
Every read takes no owner-session lock at all.
consequences: Ordinary reads remain unordered after serialized session admission, whereas uploaded-file reads wait under the same import-before-session locking obligation as uploaded-file changes.

topics.topic: Event defining the start and lock-order position of an expiry pass
questions: What event counts as the expiry pass beginning and places that pass relative to owner requests on the import and session locks?

quotes:
`module:owner_sessions`. The pass, every 60 seconds from the start, that
ends every session that has reached a limit (A13 rule 2).

The pass alone
ends sessions by their limits: it takes the import lock, reads
`clock.monotonic_reading` once, and decides every session by that one
reading, in the order of their sign-in, each under its own lock, so the
order decides nothing. Its turn on a session's lock comes after every change
of the session admitted before the pass began, which completes first with
the confirmation and the upload it may need (A13 rule 2).

In order: `configuration.load_configuration`;
`backups.probe_backup_location`; `store.open_store`; the owner interface's
listener and then, unless the start is owner-only, the service API's, each
at its address in the loaded configuration (A17 rule 1); then the surfaces answer; then two
passes: `owner_sessions.end_expired_sessions` every imported
`SESSION_PASS_SECONDS` and, except in an owner-only start,
`backups.run_daily_backup_if_due` every imported `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS`, each
from the start as Conventions, "Passes", says.
judgement.why: The pass is the invocation of `owner_sessions.end_expired_sessions`, so it begins when that scheduled public operation starts; it then enters the import lock and each session lock, behind every change admitted before that invocation began.
options: The pass begins and enters ordering when its scheduled invocation starts.
The pass begins when it acquires the session-table lock and takes its reading.
The pass is ordered only by its later per-lock queue entries.
consequences: Every change admitted before the expiry-pass invocation begins completes before the pass's turn on that session lock; requests admitted after the invocation began receive no such guarantee.
